name: Kanna Komuten
description: Kanna Komuten — a machiya renovation carpenter theme built on split screens, with a formal top header: the workshop name and tagline on the left, the Request a survey button on the right, and on wide screens the menu as a fixed sumi-ink side rail of numbered entries down the left edge (an overlay menu on phones and tablets). Ukon turmeric yellow (#FABF14) is the main colour: the hero half, the workshop band, every page head and the overlay menu are solid turmeric fields set in sumi ink. The hero is a full-bleed 35mm film photograph of a machiya under renovation running edge to edge, with the left half covered by the turmeric text panel; a cut-out hand plane sits on the seam and breaks out over the photograph and the hero bottom edge. Split-screen layout throughout: recent work as a text half beside a tall photograph, the workshop band as a turmeric half with the founding year in giant type beside a half of three photographs, projects as split rows, and every page head as a turmeric half beside a full-height photograph. Every picture is a photorealistic film-grain photograph (50mm, natural side light, fine grain, faded colour graded toward turmeric). Zen Kaku Gothic Antique for display, Schibsted Grotesk for reading, Noto Sans TC for Traditional Chinese headings. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
deviation: None: built exactly to design-plan.json row b4-4 (split-screen, full-bleed hero, side-rail nav, real-photography, film-grain, ukon #FABF14, Zen Kaku Gothic Antique + Schibsted Grotesk, business-services). The hero is full-bleed as planned; because the image column is real-photography, the full-bleed picture is a film photograph rather than an illustration. A formal top header: workshop name and tagline on the left, the Request a survey button on the right; from 1100 px the menu is a fixed sumi-ink side rail of numbered entries down the left edge (vertical entries in Chinese and Japanese), an overlay menu on phones and tablets. Split screen: the hero, recent work, the workshop band, projects and every page head are two halves, a turmeric or text half and a photograph half. Break-frame: the cut-out hand plane (transparent WebP) sits on the seam between the turmeric hero half and the full-bleed photograph and breaks out over both and over the hero bottom edge into the workshop board; the same cut-out breaks over the top edge of the turmeric workshop band on its split seam and over the seam and bottom edge of every page head. Traditional Chinese headings use a bundled Noto Sans TC Bold subset (gothic, matching Zen Kaku Gothic Antique).
